title: Dedicated→Hosted: token-bucket grace window and variant-fallback arbiter
creator: Rishi Kapoor
description: Implement a token-bucket based grace window ("grace window" hereafter) and an arbiter service that governs: (1) when requests may spill from Dedicated capacity to Hosted, (2) staged model-variant demotions during overload, and (3) region-aware tier routing constraints. The goal is deterministic, observable spill behavior with bounded error amplification for latency-sensitive tenants. This ticket covers spec, runtime changes to the routing layer, a lightweight arbiter implementation, and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Routing arbiter exposes token-bucket metrics per-tenant and region in Console with 1s granularity
During a controlled Dedicated saturation test, at least 99% of requests are served from Dedicated until per-tenant bucket depletion, then spillover begins according to configured ratios
When variant fallback triggers, we never demote more than N variant tiers within a 60s sliding window (N configurable; default 1)
No user-visible error rate increase >0.5% in canary cohort compared to baseline
End-to-end tracing shows deterministic path markings: dedicated-serve | grace-spill | hosted-fallback
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
1) Per-tenant-per-region token buckets maintained in orchestrator cache with two counters: reserve_tokens and burst_tokens. Reserve_tokens refill slowly (steady SLA-preservation), burst_tokens cover short spikes. Requests consult the arbiter before routing: if reserve_tokens>0 route Dedicated; else if burst_tokens>0 consume burst and route Dedicated with metric tag 'grace-consumed'; otherwise evaluate hosted fallback policy.
2) Hosted fallback decisions honor tenant tier and variant compatibility. The arbiter will map model variants to fallback tiers (e.g., v1-quantized -> hosted-compatible-quantized). If shard-local Dedicated variants are incompatible, arbiter permits region-variant translation or sends to hosted variant with an enacted quality-scan score threshold.
3) Implement soft-throttles to avoid thundering spill: when global hosted intake rate exceeds X% of region capacity (configurable), arbiter rate-limits spill for non-critical tenants and preferentially routes high-priority tenants to keep SLOs intact.
4) Telemetry: emit bucket level metrics (tokens_left, refill_rate, last_refill_ts) and decision traces to tracing pipeline. Add percentile latency and token consumption heatmaps to Console.
5) Backstop: if hosted variants fall below quality threshold or capacity, automated rollback routes spillback attempts to Dedicated retry (with exponential backoff) or degrade to cheaper variant with explicit flagging.
testing_plan:
Test matrix:
- Unit tests for token-bucket arithmetic and concurrent consumption (simulate 1k rps per tenant).
- Integration harness: synthetic tenants across three regions with mixed traffic profiles; run Dedicated saturation scenarios and assert spill behavior.
- Chaos test: kill 1/3 Dedicated nodes mid-spill to confirm arbiter clamps bursts and prevents overload of hosted pool.
- Quality regression: run prompt set against fallback variant and measure completion BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity thresholds.
- Load canary: route 2% of production traffic for 48 hours, monitor errors and latency.
Links: GitHub test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/simtests/pulls/112
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated behind tenant opt-in. 2) Internal canary tenants (team infra + three pilot customers) at 2% traffic. 3) Expand to 10% after 48h with health checks. 4) Full rollout region-by-region with kill-switches and per-tenant tunables (burst_tokens, refill_rate). 5) Post-rollout: 7-day monitoring window with automated regression alerts to oncall.
risks: If token refill rates are misconfigured we may either underutilize Dedicated capacity (too conservative) or cause hosted amplification (too permissive)
Model-variant translation may introduce quality regressions; need robust per-variant eval and automated rollback
Arbiter as a central component increases blast radius if it becomes a bottleneck; ensure horizontal scaling and sharding by tenant hash
Telemetry volume increases due to per-tenant token metrics; budget retention and sampling strategy required
